name: GCSE German (AQA 8662), Higher tier
material_vintage: AQA GCSE German (8662) specification, first teaching from September 2024, linked from aqa.org.uk/8662 and itemised on 2026-09-27: all three themes (People and lifestyle; Popular culture; Communication and the world around us) and their nine topics, a representative Higher-tier grammar list drawn from the full 3.2 Grammar section (Foundation content plus the Higher-tier additions: genitive case, imperfect narrative, imperative, infinitive constructions, man-passive avoidance, conditional, superlatives and derivational morphology), and the exam-skill content of all four papers. This course is built to Higher-tier demand throughout (see the tiering notice). Assessment: four linear papers, each 25% of the GCSE, all sat at the same tier in the same series -- Paper 1 Listening (Higher: 45 minutes, 50 marks, Section A in English/Section B in German, plus a dictation of at least 30 words); Paper 2 Speaking, teacher-conducted (Higher: 10-12 minutes plus 15 minutes' supervised preparation, 50 marks: role-play 10, reading aloud with four compulsory questions 15, photo-card description and unprepared conversation 25); Paper 3 Reading (Higher: 1 hour, 50 marks, including translation from German into English of at least 50 words); Paper 4 Writing (Higher: 1 hour 15 minutes, 50 marks: translation into German of at least 50 words 10, structured writing of about 90 words 15, open-ended writing of about 150 words 25). Stage tests and the mock are original materials in AQA's style.
level_source: RQF Level 2 (GCSE, grades 1-9), per Ofqual's Register of Regulated Qualifications listing for this specification

learner_notices.text: AQA GCSE German is tiered: Foundation (grades 1-5) and Higher (grades 4-9); all four papers must be taken at the same tier in the same series. This course is built to Higher-tier demand throughout, as the more complete option -- it therefore also covers everything examined at Foundation tier. If you are entered for Foundation tier, your teacher can tell you which structures (marked 'Higher tier' in the grammar stages, e.g. the genitive case, the imperfect for narrative, and translation into German) go beyond what you will be examined on, though they will not harm your Foundation preparation.

AQA replaced the previous GCSE German specification (8668) with this one (8662) for first teaching in September 2024; 8668 is now a legacy specification. Check with your teacher or aqa.org.uk which specification and exam series you are actually entered for.

The speaking exam is conducted by a teacher and marked by AQA; this course prepares you with practice conversations but cannot hold the real test. Listening practice here uses German passages you read aloud or have read to you; add authentic audio from German, Austrian and Swiss sources where you can.

AQA's 3.2 Grammar section is long and highly detailed (compound-noun formation, every plural pattern, every preposition, sound-symbol correspondences, and more). This course's sixteen grammar points give a Higher-tier-representative working grammar built from that section, covering every grammar area AQA lists (cases, verb-second/verb-final word order, separable verbs, modal verbs, adjective endings, and the Higher-tier additions) with the highest-frequency patterns and examples, rather than reproducing every minor spelling rule and irregular form -- your teacher's own materials and the vocabulary list (Appendix 2) fill in the rest.
